newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PAWN ENDS PLAN TO BUY UNION PAWN.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PAWN ENDS PLAN TO BUY UNION PAWN.

text.p: U.S. Pawn Inc said Monday it ended negotiations to buy Union Pawn of Los Angeles and said it will postpone buying additional pawn shops.
The company said it will instead focus on integrating the operations of its recent Nevada and Nebraska acquisitions and on reducing general and administrative expenses.
U.S. Pawn also said its vice president of operations Jack Simon will become chief financial officer and chief operating officer. Simon replaces Charles Van Gundy.

"The CEO felt combining the two positions (chief financial officer and chief operating officer) would help reduce costs, so he replaced Van Gundy with somebody from within the company (Simon)," a company spokesman said.

U.S. Pawn said in a statement it expected its ending plans to buy more pawn shops will reduce employee and management salaries and prevent shareholder dilution caused by issuing additional shares to pay for the acquisitions.
The company owns and operates 18 pawn shops in Colorado, Wyoming, Nevada and Nebraska. Its stock traded at 2-3/16, down 1/8.
